howTo: Enter the piston bore diameter and stroke length in millimetres (mm).
Select single-acting (compression on one stroke per revolution) or double-acting (compression on both forward and return strokes).
Enter the operating speed in rpm.
Enter the estimated volumetric efficiency (1–120 %). Typical reciprocating compressors achieve 65–85 % under nominal conditions.
Review geometric displacement (cc/rev, L/rev), geometric flow rate (L/min), and efficiency-adjusted delivery (L/min).
formula: V_geom = (π/4) · D² · S · n_cyl · f_act | Q_geom = V_geom [L/rev] · rpm | Q_adj = Q_geom · (η_v / 100) | f_act = 1 (single-acting), 2 (double-acting)

examples.title: Single-stage single-acting compressor
examples.description: A single-cylinder single-acting compressor with an 80 mm bore and 60 mm stroke running at 1 450 rpm with 80 % volumetric efficiency.
notes: Ideal geometric flow is 436.8 L/min; at 80 % volumetric efficiency the delivery is 349.4 L/min.

examples.title: Two-cylinder double-acting compressor
examples.description: A two-cylinder double-acting compressor with a 100 mm bore, 80 mm stroke, running at 960 rpm with 75 % volumetric efficiency.
notes: Double-acting mode uses ideal factor f_act = 2 without deducting piston rod area.
For precision rod-deducted capacity, refer to manufacturer datasheets.

commonMistakes: Equating geometric displacement with Free Air Delivery (FAD) without accounting for clearance volume or pressure ratio.
Assuming double-acting cylinders deliver exactly double the volume while ignoring rod volume on the crank end.
Entering rotational speed in rad/s or Hz instead of rpm.
assumptions: Geometric piston displacement is based on ideal cylindrical cylinder swept volume.
Double-acting mode treats both stroke faces with equal bore area; rod cross-section is not deducted.
Volumetric efficiency is applied as an overall scalar multiplier to geometric delivery.
Inlet air pressure, temperature, and relative humidity corrections are omitted in this geometric model.
